title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding transforms categorical variables into binary vectors. Each category becomes a column, and a row has a $$1$$ in the column corresponding to its category and 0s elsewhere.

title: Columns After One-Hot Encoding
text: Consider how many unique values are in the 'sex' and $$'embark_{town'}$$ columns. Each unique value will become a separate column in the one-hot encoded matrix.

title: Counting Unique Values
text: The 'sex' column has $$2$$ unique values: male and female. The $$'embark_{town'}$$ column has $$4$$ unique values: Southampton, Cherbourg, Queenstown, London, and Oxford.

title: Total Columns in Design Matrix
text: After one-hot encoding, the 'sex' column contributes $$2$$ columns, and the $$'embark_{town'}$$ column contributes $$4$$ columns. Adding these to the original columns gives the total number of columns in the design matrix.
